title: The Option That Was Mistyped: A Command Line That Says What Is Wrong, and Does Not Exit From Inside a Test

questions.question: QCommandLineParser is given --port abc. What does parse() return?
options: true: to the parser every value is text
questions.explanation: Qt accepted it, and as a number it is 0.

questions.question: --port 1 --port 2 is given. What does value() return?
options: 2, the last, and values() has both

questions.question: Why is parse() used and not process()?
options: process() prints the error and ends the program, which ends a test run

questions.question: A message says: --port must be a whole number from 1 to 65535, not abc. What makes it good?
options: It names the option, the rule and the value
It has a number in it
questions.explanation: All 11 messages named what was wrong.

questions.question: --help is given with a bad port. Is the line good?
options: Yes: help is asked for, and nothing else on the line is checked
questions.explanation: The help flag was set and the line was good.

questions.question: Where does the default of an option appear in the help of Qt?
options: Nowhere: the description has to say it
questions.explanation: Each description says default 5000 and so on.
